# cado's own default cofactorization strategy, benched for fbb = 25.
#
# test_strategy_cado reads it with -fm, in order to compare that strategy
# against the ones build_cofactoring_strategies computes. The parameters are
# those of the RSA-155 example in sieve/strategies/README: lim = 16777216,
# so fbb = ceil(log2(lim+1)) = 25, and lpb = 29, so nb_curves(29, 90) = 13
# and the file holds 3 + 13 = 16 methods, which is the count
# test_strategy_cado expects.
#
# The method list is PM1 315/2205, PP1-27 525/3255, ECM-M12 105/3255,
# ECM-B12 315/5355, then twelve ECM-M12 curves with B1 += sqrt(B1) and B2
# rounded to (2k+1)*105. It was benched with
#
#   bench_cofactoring_methods -in <that list> -p -t -lb 25 -N 10000 -seed 1
#
# which takes about 100 seconds. The timings in the last four columns were
# measured on one machine and do not come out the same on another; that is
# what makes this a pinned file rather than a generated one.
#
# That list came from a fork of facul_strategy_oneside::default_strategy()
# which had drifted from it twice over: B2 = 17*B1 where the live code uses
# 50*B1, and MONTY12/BRENT12 where the live code names MONTYTWED12. The
# fork is gone; this file is what it produced, so it describes a strategy
# that is not cado's current default, and regenerating it from
# default_strategy() would not reproduce these lines.
